content.content:
Frame Job (the `com.kgalligan.FrameJob` domain). Keys are never stored
there.

## Where Frame Job keeps its files

Frame Job's own folder is `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/`. It is
created only when something first needs it, at a mode only you can open; if
you have already set the folder's permissions yourself, Frame Job leaves them
alone.

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `…/Frame Job/assemblyai-key` | Your AssemblyAI key. |
| `…/Frame Job/anthropic-key` | Your Anthropic key. |
| `…/Frame Job/spend.jsonl` | The spend ledger: one line per assistant response, with its time, model, token counts and estimated dollars. It never holds your key or the conversation. |
| `…/Frame Job/anthropic-prices.json` | The assistant's cached copy of the price table it uses for that estimate. |
| `…/Frame Job/ExportPresets.json` | Your named export presets. |
| `…/Frame Job/Rewrapped/` | Movies Frame Job converted or repackaged from files macOS could not open. A project refers to these files; moving them leaves the media missing until you relink. |
| `…/Frame Job/Agent/agent.sock` | The local socket MCP clients connect to, created at every launch. |
| `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings/` | Screen recordings and voice-overs, named by date and time (for example `Screen Recording 2026-09-10 at 14.03.22`; a voice-over is `Voice-over 2026-10-02 at 09.15.04.m4a`). |

Projects themselves are `.framejob` packages wherever you save them, and hold
their own caches (see [Projects and media](projects-and-media.md)).

### How keys are stored

Each key is a plain file, readable and writable only by your user account
(mode `0600`). It is written to a temporary name and renamed into place, so
it never exists with looser permissions and is never half-written. Keys are
never put in macOS preferences, never logged, never passed as a launch
argument and never shown in the window again. Frame Job does not use the
Keychain. Anything running as your user account can read these files, so
treat your Mac account as the protection.

### Keys from the environment

If no key is stored, Frame Job falls back to an environment variable, which
is useful when you launch it from a terminal:

| Key | Variable |
|---|---|
| Anthropic (Assistant) | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` |
| AssemblyAI (Transcription) | `RC_ASSEMBLYAI_KEY` |

A stored key always wins over the variable. An empty variable counts as no
key. **Verify** checks the variable's key when nothing is typed or stored.

## Limits

- Settings has no MCP mirror. An agent cannot set or read a key, the model,
  the region or Background render.
- There is no button to forget the remembered convert-on-import answer. To
  be asked again, run `defaults delete com.kgalligan.FrameJob RCFFmpegImport`
  in Terminal while Frame Job is closed.
- Converting on import needs `ffmpeg` and `ffprobe`. Frame Job looks for them
  on `PATH` and in `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`, `/opt/local/bin`,
## What a `.framejob` package holds

A package is a folder that the Finder shows as one file:

| Inside | What it is |
|---|---|
| `project.json` | The edit itself: canvas, media list, tracks, clips, markers. The only thing a package needs in order to open. |
| `cache/` | Things Frame Job can rebuild: filmstrip thumbnails, waveforms, the voice-detection and sync analyses, transcripts, reversed clips, speed-ramp audio, the shot changes, faces, sound events and subjects (people and salient regions) found for an agent, the faces and subjects drawn by View ▸ Show Subjects, and the person masks found for one or made for a clip with Remove Background (`cache/analysis/`; a minute of 1080p video's masks take about 62 MB). A package with a missing or damaged `cache/` still opens and just redraws. |
| `media/` | Only after **Consolidate Media…**: copies of the footage (see [Consolidate Media](#consolidate-media)). |
| `graphics/` | Only once you add a graphic: graphic modules, their fonts, images and kept versions. See [Graphics](graphics.md). |

**Media is referenced, not copied.** By default a project remembers where each file lives (its path and a Finder bookmark, so a moved file is often found again) and reads it from there. The package stays small, but it depends on the footage staying put. Consolidate Media is how you make a package hold everything it needs.

Caches are built in the background after an open, an import or a relink, and the timeline fills in as they finish. Frame Job builds at most two files' sound caches at a time, on threads of their own, so importing many long files at once does not hold up playback or a speed ramp's sound. A cache that already matches its file is never rebuilt. Moving, copying or consolidating the package keeps its caches. Until an untitled project is first saved, its caches live in a temporary folder; the first save copies them in.

*Transcripts* cost money to rebuild when they came from the cloud engine, so treat `cache/transcripts/` as worth keeping. See [Captions](captions.md).

## The Document tab: canvas settings
## Bringing files in

### What Frame Job reads

| Kind | Files |
|---|---|
| Movies | MOV, MP4, M4V and other containers macOS plays: H.264, HEVC, ProRes, MJPEG and MPEG-4 video; VP9 Profile 0 and 2 in MP4; AV1 on an M3 or later Mac. |
| WebM and Matroska | `.webm` and `.mkv` with VP9, AV1, H.264 or HEVC video and Opus, Vorbis or AAC sound (see below). |
| Sound | M4A (AAC, ALAC), MP3, WAV and AIFF everywhere. Other formats macOS plays, such as CAF and FLAC, import when dropped on the Media tab. |
| Pictures | PNG, JPEG and HEIC everywhere. TIFF, GIF, BMP, HEIF and WebP also import when dropped on the Media tab. |
| LUTs | `.cube` 3D LUTs, applied as a clip's look or as a file's Camera Log. See [Color grading](color-grading.md). |

Caption files (`.srt`) are not media: bring them in with **File ▸ Import Captions…**. See [Captions](captions.md).

### Add Media

**File ▸ Add Media…** (⇧⌘I), or the Media tab's **Add Media…** button, opens a panel for one or more files. Every file is checked first. The readable ones are added to the Media tab together as one undo step ("Add Media", or "Add 3 Media Files"). A file that cannot be read shows an alert naming it, and the rest are still added. Adding a file that is already in the list changes nothing.

Adding puts files in the Media tab, **not** on the timeline. Place them from there (see [Putting media on the timeline](#putting-media-on-the-timeline)).

You can also drag files from the Finder onto the **Media tab**. That adds them to this project. A Finder drop anywhere else on the window (the canvas, the timeline) *opens* the file as a project of its own, as a drop on the Dock icon does.

*Agents:* `import_media` (takes a `path`; answers the new media id and what the check found: kind, duration, display size, frame rate, video/audio/alpha). `add_media` is the raw op behind it, taking a descriptor you supply.

### WebM and Matroska files

macOS cannot play WebM or MKV directly, so Frame Job copies the video and sound streams into a movie, without re-encoding, the first time you add or open one. The copy goes into `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/Rewrapped/`; your original is left where it is.

- There is no question to answer. A copy that takes more than a second shows a small **Copying Movie** window with its progress, and **Cancel** stops it and adds nothing.
- Before copying, Frame Job checks the disk has room. If it does not: "Not enough free space to open *file*: its video and sound need about *size* on "*volume*", which has *size* free. Nothing was copied."
- The copy keeps the colour the file states: HLG, HDR10 (PQ), or a BT.709, BT.601 or BT.2020 SDR picture, read from the file's colour information or, for VP9, from the video itself. A file that states none is shown as macOS reads it.
- Importing the same file again reuses the copy.
- The media keeps the original's name, and its tooltip on the Media tab says where the copy lives.
- If the copy is later deleted, or moved to the Trash, the project makes it again from the original the next time it opens. If that copy is cancelled or fails, the file shows as missing (a slate, the **missing** badge, Relink…) until the next open tries again.
- Frame Job never deletes anything from the Rewrapped folder, which every project shares, so copies pile up there. You can clear it: WebM and MKV copies are made again on the next open (ffmpeg conversions are not; see below).
- **Consolidate Media** copies the copy, not the WebM, into the package's `media/` folder, and the row's tooltip then says it was copied into this project's package.

A stream the built-in copy cannot carry (FLAC, MP3, AC-3, MPEG-2 and similar) is refused with a sentence naming it. If you have ffmpeg installed, Frame Job then offers to help (next section).

### Files macOS cannot open, and ffmpeg

When macOS refuses a file and `ffmpeg` and `ffprobe` are both installed on this Mac, Frame Job asks before doing anything. It looks in your `PATH` first, then in `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`, `/opt/local/bin`, `/usr/bin` and `/bin`; to use one particular build, run `defaults write com.kgalligan.FrameJob RCFFmpegPath /path/to/ffmpeg` (its `ffprobe` is taken from the same folder when one is there). The alert, "Frame Job cannot open *file*.", says what it would cost: a quick **Repackage** that copies the streams, or a **Convert** that re-encodes, with the size and the time it would take. Tick **Do this automatically from now on** to have your answer remembered: always, if you accept, or never, if you cancel. The converted file goes into the same Rewrapped folder, and the original is untouched. A conversion that fails shows "Could not convert *file* with ffmpeg: *reason*". Unlike a WebM copy, a conversion that is later deleted is not made again when the project opens: the media stays missing until you relink it. Frame Job does not ship ffmpeg; without one, this step never appears. To be asked again after ticking "Do this automatically", see [Settings](settings.md#limits).

An agent's import never shows this question. Unless you have chosen "always", the file is refused instead.

### Files that are refused

- **A codec this Mac cannot decode** is refused at import with a sentence naming it, for example "*file* is AV1 video, which needs an M3 or later Mac." or "*file* is VP9 Profile 1 video, which this Mac cannot decode; VP9 Profiles 0 and 2 import." VP8 is refused the same way. A file in a codec this Mac does decode still imports even when some of its data is damaged.
- **A `.cube` the LUT reader cannot read** is refused naming the line and the problem, for example "“Film.cube” is not a LUT Frame Job reads: line 2: LUT_3D_SIZE 200 is outside 2–65."
- "Could not read *file*." means the file is damaged or not a format Frame Job reads.
- "*file* has no video or audio the app can open." means the file holds neither.
- "Timed out reading *file*." means the check took longer than 30 seconds, usually because the file is on a stalled network volume.

## Limits

- Consolidate Media needs a saved project.
- Canvas width and height are even numbers from 16 to 16384 px.
- A project holds at most 4,096 clips and 64 tracks (counting those inside nests), 1,024 markers and 1,024 media files, with nests up to 8 deep.
- The Add Media… and Open panels list movies, M4A, MP3, WAV, AIFF, PNG, JPEG, HEIC and (Add Media… only) `.cube`. Other sound and picture formats import only by a drop on the Media tab, or through `import_media`.
- `.cube` files are imported, not opened: File ▸ Open… does not take one, and a `.cube` dropped on the window or the Dock is not imported. Use Add Media… or a drop on the Media tab.
- A project file that is damaged or out of range fails to open with a message naming the problem; the package is not rewritten. A package saved by a newer Frame Job reports "project format version *N* is newer than this build understands (version *M*); update Frame Job to open it". A package with no readable `project.json` reports "*name* does not contain a readable project.json."

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

content.content:
---
title: "WebM and Matroska files"
description: "How Frame Job brings in .webm and .mkv files by copying their streams into a movie, what the copy can carry, and where the copies live."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

macOS won't open a WebM or MKV file directly, so Frame Job copies its video and sound into a QuickTime movie the first time you bring one in. Nothing is re-encoded, so no quality is lost, and your original stays where it is.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['File ▸ Add Media…', 'File ▸ Open…']}
  keys={['⇧⌘I', '⌘O']}
  where="Drag to the Media tab"
  tools={['import_media', 'open_project', 'relink_media']}
/>

## How a file is rewrapped

Add, open or relink the file as you would any other. There's no question to answer: the copy starts by itself, and the clip then plays from the copy.

content.content:
---
title: "Recording files and formats"
description: "Where recordings are saved, how their files are named, what format each one is, and why a still screen gives a low frame rate."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Every recording is a set of ordinary files in one folder, so they outlast any project they land in. This page lists what each recording writes and in what format.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ New Recording…"
  keys="⌥⌘N"
  tools="record_screen"
/>

## Where recordings are saved

Recordings go in `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings/`, which Frame Job creates the first time it needs it. The panel's footnote shows the folder before you start.

They're never stored inside the project package. A recording is original footage, so it survives even if you never save the project it opened in, and undoing a landing leaves its files on disk. To carry recordings into the package, use [Consolidate Media](/projects/consolidate-media/).

## What each recording writes

| File | Example name | Format |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Screen movie](#the-screen-movie) | `Screen Recording 2026-09-10 at 14.03.22.mov` | QuickTime movie, HEVC or H.264 |
| [Its microphone](#the-microphone-file) | `Screen Recording 2026-09-10 at 14.03.22 (Microphone).m4a` | Mono 48 kHz AAC |
| [Its cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/) | `Screen Recording 2026-09-10 at 14.03.22.fjcursor` | Frame Job's own |
| [Voice-over](#voice-over-files) | `Voice-over 2026-10-02 at 09.15.04.m4a` | Mono 48 kHz AAC |
| [Camera on its own](#camera-files) | `Camera Recording 2026-10-26 at 17.14.33.mov` | QuickTime movie, HEVC or H.264 |
| [Camera beside the screen](#camera-files) | `Screen Recording 2026-10-26 at 17.14.33 (Camera).mov` | QuickTime movie, HEVC or H.264 |

## How files are named

A file is named by the date and time it began, on a 24-hour clock in your Mac's time zone.

A [pause](/recording/pause-and-stop/) ends a file and a resume starts a new one, so each stretch of a paused recording is its own set of files, named by the time that stretch began.

When a name is already taken, Frame Job adds ` (2)`, ` (3)` and so on.

## The screen movie

A screen recording is a QuickTime `.mov` in HEVC where your Mac offers it, otherwise H.264. Its size comes from the panel's **Size** row, or a picked window's own size.

With **System Audio** on, the movie has one stereo 48 kHz sound track of what your Mac plays. Frame Job's own sound is left out, so playing your timeline during a recording doesn't get into it.

The microphone is never a track of the movie.

## The microphone file

**Cancel** stops between files, so the sheet shows "Stopping…" until the file in progress is done. What was copied stays copied and the project points at it, and the rest keep pointing at the originals. The project always opens. Run the command again to copy the rest.

## When it finishes

The sheet says what happened, offers **Show in Finder** and **Close**, and the changes to the project are one undo step called **Consolidate Media**. **Show in Finder** shows the package's `media` folder and closes the sheet.

| The sheet says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "Copied 4 files (2.1 GB) into the package." | How many files it copied, cursor files included. |
| "No files needed copying." | Nothing was copied, and only links were corrected. |
| "Stopped before the rest." | You chose **Cancel**. |
| "2 files could not be copied." | Those files keep pointing at their originals, so every clip still plays. The first file's reason shows underneath. |
| "1 missing file was left alone — relink intro.mov." | See [Missing files](#missing-files). It names up to three. |
| "1 cursor file was missing and left alone." | See [Cursor files](#cursor-files). |

## What gets copied

### Names and duplicates

- Two different files with the same name are kept apart, as `intro.mov` and `intro-2.mov`. Names are compared without regard to case, and a name already in the `media` folder counts as taken.
- Two media entries for one file share a single copy.
- Files already inside the package aren't copied again.

### Missing files

A missing file can't be copied, so it's left alone and the sheet names it. [Relink it](/projects/relink-media/) and consolidate again.

With nothing to do, Frame Job doesn't open the sheet. It shows an alert reading "Nothing to consolidate." and why:

- "Every file this project uses is already inside the package."
- "Every file this project can find is already inside the package. 2 missing files need relinking first."

### LUTs

[LUTs](/color/luts/) are consolidated like footage.

## What each way takes

The **Add Media…** and **File ▸ Open…** panels only let you pick the types they list. To bring in anything else, drop it on the Media tab.

| Files | **Add Media…** | **File ▸ Open…**, or a drop on the window or the Dock | A drop on the Media tab |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Movies | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| M4A, MP3, WAV and AIFF | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| PNG, JPEG and HEIC | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| `.cube` LUTs | Yes | No | Yes |
| TIFF, GIF, BMP, HEIF and WebP | No | No | Yes |
| CAF, FLAC and other sound macOS plays | No | No | Yes |

A `.cube` is imported, never opened. It sits in the Media tab and you apply it to clips as a [look](/color/luts/), or to a file as its [camera log](/hdr/log-luts/). It never goes on the timeline.

Caption files aren't media. Bring an `.srt` in with [Import Captions](/captions/import-captions/). Every format and codec Frame Job reads is listed in [Supported file formats](/reference/file-formats/).

## Drop files to open them

Drag from the Finder onto a project window, the Welcome window or the Dock icon. Each file opens as a document of its own:

- A `.framejob` package opens that project.
- A media file opens as a fresh untitled project built around it, so several files make several projects.

Only projects and the types **File ▸ Open…** lists are taken: MOV, MP4, M4V and other movies, M4A, MP3, WAV, AIFF, PNG, JPEG and HEIC. Anything else is ignored.

:::caution
A drop on a project window doesn't add to that project. To add a file to the project you have open, drop it on the [Media tab](/projects/import-media/). Anywhere else in the window, the timeline and preview included, the drop opens a new project.
:::

## Open a project that's already open

Opening a saved project that's already open brings its window forward. It doesn't open a second copy.

That's for saved projects. A movie opened as an untitled project has no file of its own yet, so opening the same movie again makes a second untitled project.

## Open a project from another version

A project saved by any earlier version of Frame Job opens. It's brought up to the current format as it opens, one format at a time, and the next save writes it in the current format.

A project saved by a newer Frame Job won't open. The message gives both versions and asks you to update:

> project format version *N* is newer than this build understands (version *M*); update Frame Job to open it

32:| [HLG or PQ still](#hdr-stills) | Converted as a video of the same kind is | Drawn in its own colour, as HDR |
37:Ordinary Rec. 709 video, video with no colour labels, stills and screen recordings are drawn as they are in an SDR project.
91:## HDR stills
93:A still labelled HLG or PQ is treated as HDR, the way a video of the same kind is, rather than being read as SDR. Bring it in with **File ▸ Add Media…** (<kbd>⇧⌘I</kbd>) as you would any picture. This works for PNG, HEIC and AVIF, which keep their colour space and depth.

---
title: "Where Frame Job keeps its files"
description: "Find your API keys, spend ledger, export presets, converted movies, recordings and projects on your Mac, and see how Frame Job protects your keys."
---

Frame Job keeps its own data in one folder in your Library and your recordings in your Movies folder. Projects live wherever you save them. Use this page when you want to back something up, clear something out, or check what's stored on your Mac.

## What's where

In this table, `…/Frame Job/` is short for `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/`.

| Path | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `…/Frame Job/assemblyai-key` | Your [AssemblyAI key](#key-files) |
| `…/Frame Job/anthropic-key` | Your [Anthropic key](#key-files) |
| `…/Frame Job/spend.jsonl` | The [spend ledger](#the-spend-ledger) |
| `…/Frame Job/anthropic-prices.json` | The assistant's [cached price table](#the-spend-ledger) |
| `…/Frame Job/ExportPresets.json` | Your [named export presets](#export-presets) |
| `…/Frame Job/Rewrapped/` | [Movies Frame Job copied or converted](#rewrapped-copies) from files macOS could not open |
| `…/Frame Job/Agent/agent.sock` | The [local socket](#the-agent-socket) MCP clients connect to |
| `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings/` | [Screen recordings, camera recordings and voice-overs](#recordings) |
| Wherever you save them | [Projects](#projects), as `.framejob` packages |

## The Application Support folder

Frame Job's own folder is `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/`. The Finder hides your Library, so to open it choose **Go ▸ Go to Folder…** in the Finder and paste the path.

Frame Job makes the folder when something first needs it, and each folder under it only when there's something to put there. You won't find empty folders for features you've never used.

Each folder it makes has mode `0700`, so only your user account can open it. If you've already set a folder's permissions yourself, Frame Job leaves them alone.

## Key files

Your keys are two files in that folder:

| File | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `assemblyai-key` | Your AssemblyAI key, for cloud transcription. See [Your AssemblyAI key](/captions/assemblyai-key/). |
| `anthropic-key` | Your Anthropic key, for the assistant. It goes to the assistant's helper when a conversation starts, and nowhere else. See [Set up the Assistant](/assistant/set-up/). |

Save, replace and remove keys in Settings. A file that's empty, or holds only spaces, counts as no key.

## How keys are stored

Each key is a plain file that only your user account can read or write (mode `0600`). It's written to a temporary name and renamed into place, so it never exists with looser permissions and is never half-written.

- put in macOS preferences
- logged
- passed as a launch argument
- passed to an agent tool, or returned by one
- shown in the Settings window again

:::

| --- | --- |
| Anthropic (Assistant) | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` |
| AssemblyAI (Transcription) | `RC_ASSEMBLYAI_KEY` |

Your named export presets are in `ExportPresets.json`. If that file is missing or damaged, the presets list is empty and nothing else is affected. See [Export presets](/export/presets/).

The `Rewrapped/` folder holds movies Frame Job made from files macOS could not open: [WebM and MKV copies](/projects/webm-and-matroska/) and [ffmpeg conversions](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/). Your originals stay where they are.

MCP clients connect through `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/Agent/agent.sock`, a local socket Frame Job creates at every launch. See [The helper and the socket](/mcp/helper-and-socket/).

## Recordings

Screen recordings, camera recordings and voice-overs go to `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings/`, named by date and time: `Screen Recording 2026-09-10 at 14.03.22`, or `Voice-over 2026-10-02 at 09.15.04.m4a`. The folder is made when a recording first has something to put in it.

See [Recording files and formats](/recording/files-and-formats/) for every file a recording writes.

A project is a `.framejob` package, saved wherever you choose. Each package holds its own caches, so they move with it. See [The .framejob package](/reference/framejob-package/).

View settings and other remembered choices are in the `com.kgalligan.FrameJob` preferences domain. Keys are never stored there. See [What Frame Job remembers](/reference/remembered-choices/).

- [The .framejob package](/reference/framejob-package/)
- [Supported file formats](/reference/file-formats/)
- [Settings](/reference/settings/)

---
title: "Supported file formats"
description: "Check which movies, sound files, pictures and LUTs Frame Job can bring in, what happens to transparency, rotation and odd frame rates, and which way in takes which file."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

This page lists what Frame Job can bring in, and which way in takes which file. For what it can write, see [Export formats](/export/formats/).

<AtAGlance
  menu={['File ▸ Add Media…', 'File ▸ Open…', 'File ▸ Import Captions…']}
  keys={['⇧⌘I', '⌘O']}
  where="Drag to the Media tab"
  tools={['import_media', 'import_captions']}
/>

## What Frame Job reads

| Kind | Files |
| --- | --- |
| [Movies](#movies) | MOV, MP4, M4V and other containers macOS plays |
| [WebM and Matroska](#webm-and-matroska) | `.webm` and `.mkv` |
| [Sound](#sound) | M4A, MP3, WAV and AIFF, plus CAF, FLAC and other formats macOS plays |
| [Pictures](#pictures) | PNG, JPEG and HEIC, plus TIFF, GIF, BMP, HEIF and WebP |
| [LUTs](#luts) | `.cube` 3D LUTs |

Some of these only come in by a drop on the Media tab. See [Which way in](#which-way-in).

## Movies

Frame Job reads MOV, MP4, M4V and the other containers macOS plays. What matters is the video inside:

| Video | What Frame Job does |
| --- | --- |
| H.264, HEVC, ProRes, MJPEG, MPEG-4 | Reads it. |
| VP9 in MP4 | Reads Profile 0 and Profile 2, through macOS's optional decoder. Profiles 1 and 3 don't import. |
| AV1 | Reads it on an M3 or later Mac, because it needs a hardware decoder. |
| VP8 | Doesn't import. |

Before it adds a video, Frame Job decodes its first frame, so a file nothing on this Mac can decode is left out rather than added. An alert names the codec. See [Codecs this Mac can't decode](/projects/import-media/#codecs-this-mac-cant-decode).

The check gives up after 30 seconds, which usually means a stalled network volume. See [Import errors](/projects/import-media/#import-errors).

### Movies with alpha

Frame Job detects transparency when you import a movie. It recognises ProRes 4444, ProRes 4444 XQ and QuickTime Animation, and any track flagged as containing alpha, such as HEVC with alpha.

A **VP9 with Alpha (WebM)** file keeps its picture and loses its transparency when you bring it back in. To make a transparent clip you can re-import, export ProRes 4444 or HEVC with Alpha.

### Portrait and rotated movies

A movie imports at its display size, through the file's own rotation. A portrait phone clip comes in as 1080 × 1920, not as 1920 × 1080 lying on its side.

### Variable and unusual frame rates

Frame Job takes the rate macOS reports for the video track, which gives a variable-rate file one rate too.

A rate within 0.01 fps of a standard one becomes exactly that rate: 23.976, 24, 25, 29.97, 30, 48, 50, 59.94 or 60 fps. Anything else keeps three decimals, so a 47.3 fps screen recording isn't called 48.

If the file reports no rate, Frame Job works it out from the shortest frame. With nothing to go on, it uses 30 fps.

## WebM and Matroska

macOS can't open these, so Frame Job copies the streams unchanged into a QuickTime movie, with no re-encoding. It reads `.webm` and `.mkv` files with VP9, AV1, H.264 or HEVC video and Opus, Vorbis or AAC sound.

A file is recognised by its header, not its name, and the first video track and first audio track are the ones copied. See [WebM and Matroska files](/projects/webm-and-matroska/).

## Sound

M4A (AAC and ALAC), MP3, WAV and AIFF come in every way. Other formats macOS plays, such as CAF and FLAC, come in only by a drop on the Media tab.

### Any sample rate

Sound at any rate other than 48 kHz, 96 kHz included, plays from a hidden 48 kHz copy, so it stays aligned with its place on the timeline. This is automatic. The copies live in the temporary folder, outside the project, and are made again whenever they're needed.

### MP3 gapless start

Some MP3s begin with a short stretch of encoder delay that isn't part of the recording. When macOS leaves it in, Frame Job skips it at any sample rate, so the sound starts on time. Playback, the waveform, transcription, sync and a reversed clip all skip the same amount.

This applies to MP3 files. An MP3 track inside a `.mov`, `.mp4` or `.m4a` isn't trimmed.

## Pictures

PNG, JPEG and HEIC come in every way. TIFF, GIF, BMP, HEIF and WebP come in only by a drop on the Media tab.

A picture imports as a still with no length of its own, so a clip of it can run any duration. Its transparency and EXIF orientation are honoured.

Only a GIF's first image is read, so an animated GIF imports as a still.

### Deep and HDR stills

| The still is | What Frame Job does |
| --- | --- |
| Deeper than 8 bits a component, such as a 16-bit PNG or TIFF or a 10-bit HEIC | Draws it at 16-bit float, so its levels reach the picture. See [Precision and bit depth](/hdr/precision/). |
| Labelled HLG or PQ | Treats it by its own colour instead of as SDR. Display P3, BT.709 and BT.2020 primaries are recognised. See [How sources are read](/hdr/how-sources-are-read/#hdr-stills). |
| HEIC with an HDR gain map (ISO 21496-1 or Apple's) | Shows its full HDR in an HLG project. An SDR project and every thumbnail draw the base picture. |

A frame showing a deep still is saved deep as PNG or HEIC, never as JPEG. See [Save Frame](/export/save-frame/). GIF and Animated PNG exports stay 8-bit.

## LUTs

Frame Job reads `.cube` 3D LUTs, which you apply as a clip's [look](/color/luts/) or as a file's [Camera Log](/hdr/log-luts/).

- 3D only, so a 1D LUT is refused.
- `LUT_3D_SIZE` from 2 to 65.
- At most 32 MiB.

A `.cube` is imported, not opened. **File ▸ Open…** doesn't take one, and one dropped on the window or the Dock isn't imported. Use **File ▸ Add Media…** or a drop on the Media tab.

## Caption files

An `.srt` isn't media. Bring it in with **File ▸ Import Captions…**. See [Import captions](/captions/import-captions/).

Import reads SubRip only. WebVTT can be [exported](/captions/export-captions/) but not imported.

## Which way in

The **Add Media…** and **File ▸ Open…** panels list fewer types than a drop on the Media tab takes.

| Files | **File ▸ Add Media…** | **File ▸ Open…** | A drop on the Media tab |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Movies | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| M4A, MP3, WAV and AIFF | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| PNG, JPEG and HEIC | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| `.cube` LUTs | Yes | No | Yes |
| TIFF, GIF, BMP, HEIF and WebP | No | No | Yes |
| CAF, FLAC and other sound macOS plays | No | No | Yes |

A drop on the Media tab has no type filter, so any file is tried, and an agent's import takes the same files. **File ▸ Add Media…** and a drop on the Media tab add to the open project, and **File ▸ Open…** makes a new untitled project around the file. See [Import media](/projects/import-media/) and [Drop files to open them](/projects/open-a-project/#drop-files-to-open-them).

In the Finder, **Open With ▸ Frame Job** is offered for movies, M4A, MP3, WAV, AIFF, PNG, JPEG and HEIC files. Frame Job doesn't make itself the default app for any of them.

## Related

- [Import media](/projects/import-media/)
- [Export formats](/export/formats/)
- [Convert files with ffmpeg](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/)
- [Limits](/reference/limits/)

---
title: "The .framejob package"
description: "See what a saved project holds, which parts Frame Job can rebuild and which it can't, and what happens when you move or copy a package."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A Frame Job project is one `.framejob` package: a folder the Finder shows as one file. It holds your edit, its caches and, if you ask for them, copies of your footage.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['File ▸ Save', 'File ▸ Consolidate Media…']}
  keys="⌘S"
  tools={['save_project', 'consolidate_media']}
/>

## What a package is

| Inside | What it is | Can Frame Job rebuild it? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`project.json`](#projectjson) | The edit itself | No. A package needs it to open. |
| [`cache/`](#cache) | Thumbnails, waveforms, analyses and renders | Yes, though [cloud transcripts](#transcripts-are-worth-keeping) cost money. |
| [`media/`](#media) | Copies of your footage, only after **Consolidate Media…** | No. It may be the only copy. |
| [`graphics/`](#graphics) | Graphic modules, fonts, images and kept versions, only once you add a graphic | No. |

To look inside, Control-click the package in the Finder and choose **Show Package Contents**.

A project only ever saves as a `.framejob` package. A movie or a still is a separate step: see [Export](/export/formats/) and [Save Frame](/export/save-frame/).

A save writes the new package beside the old one and swaps it in, so a crash part-way through can't leave half a package.

:::caution
A save keeps only those four things. Any other file you put inside a package is dropped at the next save, autosaves included.
:::

## `project.json`

This is the edit itself: the canvas, media list, tracks, clips and markers. It's the only thing a package needs in order to open.

A project from any earlier version of Frame Job opens, and the next save writes it in the current format. A project from a newer build won't open, and the message asks you to update Frame Job. See [Open a project from another version](/projects/open-a-project/#open-a-project-from-another-version).

| Folder | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `thumbs/` | Filmstrip thumbnails |
| `peaks/` | Waveforms |
| `loudness/` | Loudness measurements |
| `speech/` | Voice detection |
| `sync/` | The analysis for [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/) |
| `transcripts/` | [Transcripts from AssemblyAI](#transcripts-are-worth-keeping) |
| `device-transcripts/` | Words recognised on this Mac |
| `analysis/` | [On-device analysis](/projects/media-analysis/): shot changes, faces, sound events and subjects found for an agent, the faces and subjects drawn by **View ▸ Show Subjects**, and the masks for **Remove Background** |
| `reversed/` | [Reversed clips](/speed/reverse/) |
| `ramp-audio/` | Sound for [speed ramps](/speed/speed-ramps/) |
| `isolated/` | [Voice Isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/) renders |
| `voiced/` | [Voice effect](/audio/voice-effects/) renders |

Masks are the largest of these: a minute of 1080p video's masks take about 62 MB.

A transcript from AssemblyAI costs money to make again, so treat `cache/transcripts/` as worth keeping. Everything else in `cache/` rebuilds for nothing but time.

This folder exists only after [Consolidate Media…](/projects/consolidate-media/), and it holds copies of your footage. Unlike `cache/`, it may be the only copy, so don't delete it.

## `graphics/`

This folder exists once you add a [graphic](/graphics/manage-graphics/). It holds the graphic modules and these folders:

| Folder | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `fonts/` | [Fonts](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/) the graphics use |
| `assets/` | [Images](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/) the graphics use |
| `history/` | The last 10 kept versions of each module, one folder per module |

## How a package travels

Moving, copying or consolidating a package keeps its caches. Until an untitled project is first saved, its caches live in a temporary folder, and the first save copies them in.

When you open a package, any media missing from its stored path is looked for in the package's own `media/` folder under the same name. That's what lets you move a consolidated package. A working link is never replaced this way.

A referenced file that has moved is often found again through its bookmark. If it isn't, see [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/).

To take a project to another Mac, run Consolidate Media first, so the footage goes with it.

- [Save, revert and close](/projects/save-and-revert/)
- [Consolidate Media](/projects/consolidate-media/)
- [Where Frame Job keeps its files](/reference/file-locations/)

# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, Node is pinned by `.node-version`. `README.md` has the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.

</system-reminder>

---
title: "Where Frame Job keeps its files"
description: "Find your API keys, spend ledger, export presets, converted movies, recordings and projects on your Mac, and see how Frame Job protects your keys."
---

Frame Job keeps its own data in one folder in your Library and your recordings in your Movies folder. Projects live wherever you save them. Use this page when you want to back something up, clear something out, or check what's stored on your Mac.

## What's where

In this table, `…/Frame Job/` is short for `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/`.

| Path | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `…/Frame Job/assemblyai-key` | Your [AssemblyAI key](#key-files) |
| `…/Frame Job/anthropic-key` | Your [Anthropic key](#key-files) |
| `…/Frame Job/spend.jsonl` | The [spend ledger](#the-spend-ledger) |
| `…/Frame Job/anthropic-prices.json` | The assistant's [cached price table](#the-spend-ledger) |
| `…/Frame Job/ExportPresets.json` | Your [named export presets](#export-presets) |
| `…/Frame Job/Rewrapped/` | [Movies Frame Job copied or converted](#rewrapped-copies) from files macOS could not open |
| `…/Frame Job/Agent/agent.sock` | The [local socket](#the-agent-socket) MCP clients connect to |
| `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings/` | [Screen recordings, camera recordings and voice-overs](#recordings) |
| Wherever you save them | [Projects](#projects), as `.framejob` packages |

## The Application Support folder

Frame Job's own folder is `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/`. The Finder hides your Library, so to open it choose **Go ▸ Go to Folder…** in the Finder and paste the path.

Frame Job makes the folder when something first needs it, and each folder under it only when there's something to put there. You won't find empty folders for features you've never used.

Each folder it makes has mode `0700`, so only your user account can open it. If you've already set a folder's permissions yourself, Frame Job leaves them alone.

## Key files

Your keys are two files in that folder:

| File | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `assemblyai-key` | Your AssemblyAI key, for cloud transcription. See [Your AssemblyAI key](/captions/assemblyai-key/). |
| `anthropic-key` | Your Anthropic key, for the assistant. It goes to the assistant's helper when a conversation starts, and nowhere else. See [Set up the Assistant](/assistant/set-up/). |

Save, replace and remove keys in Settings. A file that's empty, or holds only spaces, counts as no key.

## How keys are stored

Each key is a plain file that only your user account can read or write (mode `0600`). It's written to a temporary name and renamed into place, so it never exists with looser permissions and is never half-written.

A key is never:

- put in macOS preferences
- logged
- passed as a launch argument
- passed to an agent tool, or returned by one
- shown in the Settings window again

:::caution
Frame Job doesn't use the Keychain. Anything running as your user account can read these files, so treat your Mac account as the protection.
:::

## Keys from the environment

If no key is stored, Frame Job falls back to an environment variable.

| Key | Variable |
| --- | --- |
| Anthropic (Assistant) | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` |
| AssemblyAI (Transcription) | `RC_ASSEMBLYAI_KEY` |

- A stored key always wins over the variable.
- An empty variable counts as no key.
- **Verify** in Settings' Transcription section checks the variable's key when nothing is typed or stored. The Assistant section has no **Verify**.
- A key from a variable isn't stored, so **Remove** stays dimmed unless you've saved one too.

In practice this only applies when you start Frame Job from a shell that sets the variable, because an app opened from the Finder or the Dock doesn't see your shell's variables.

## The spend ledger

`spend.jsonl` records one line per assistant response, with its time, model, token counts and estimated dollars. A response that was cut short is marked as one. The file never holds your key or the conversation, and only your user account can read it.

The month's spend in Settings is added up from this file. If Frame Job can't write to it, the conversation carries on and the transcript shows a note saying why.

`anthropic-prices.json` is the assistant's cached copy of the price table it uses for that estimate. It's refreshed at most once a day. See [What it costs](/assistant/cost/).

## Export presets

Your named export presets are in `ExportPresets.json`. If that file is missing or damaged, the presets list is empty and nothing else is affected. See [Export presets](/export/presets/).

## Rewrapped copies

The `Rewrapped/` folder holds movies Frame Job made from files macOS could not open: [WebM and MKV copies](/projects/webm-and-matroska/) and [ffmpeg conversions](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/). Your originals stay where they are.

A project refers to the file in this folder, not to the original. Moving one leaves the media missing until you [relink](/projects/relink-media/) it.

Every project shares this folder, and Frame Job never deletes anything from it, so copies pile up. You can clear it yourself:

- WebM and MKV copies are made again from the original the next time a project using them opens.
- ffmpeg conversions aren't. That media stays missing until you relink it.

[Consolidate Media](/projects/consolidate-media/) copies a project's rewrapped files into its package, which frees that project from this folder.

## The agent socket

MCP clients connect through `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/Agent/agent.sock`, a local socket Frame Job creates at every launch. See [The helper and the socket](/mcp/helper-and-socket/).

## Recordings

Screen recordings, camera recordings and voice-overs go to `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings/`, named by date and time: `Screen Recording 2026-09-10 at 14.03.22`, or `Voice-over 2026-10-02 at 09.15.04.m4a`. The folder is made when a recording first has something to put in it.

See [Recording files and formats](/recording/files-and-formats/) for every file a recording writes.

## Projects

A project is a `.framejob` package, saved wherever you choose. Each package holds its own caches, so they move with it. See [The .framejob package](/reference/framejob-package/).

## Preferences

View settings and other remembered choices are in the `com.kgalligan.FrameJob` preferences domain. Keys are never stored there. See [What Frame Job remembers](/reference/remembered-choices/).

## Temporary files

Files Frame Job can always make again go in macOS's temporary folder, outside any project: the caches of a project you haven't saved yet, and the [48 kHz copies](/reference/file-formats/#any-sample-rate) of sound at other sample rates. You don't need to keep them.

## Related

- [The .framejob package](/reference/framejob-package/)
- [Supported file formats](/reference/file-formats/)
- [Settings](/reference/settings/)

---
title: "Supported file formats"
description: "Check which movies, sound files, pictures and LUTs Frame Job can bring in, what happens to transparency, rotation and odd frame rates, and which way in takes which file."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

This page lists what Frame Job can bring in, and which way in takes which file. For what it can write, see [Export formats](/export/formats/).

<AtAGlance
  menu={['File ▸ Add Media…', 'File ▸ Open…', 'File ▸ Import Captions…']}
  keys={['⇧⌘I', '⌘O']}
  where="Drag to the Media tab"
  tools={['import_media', 'import_captions']}
/>

## What Frame Job reads

| Kind | Files |
| --- | --- |
| [Movies](#movies) | MOV, MP4, M4V and other containers macOS plays |
| [WebM and Matroska](#webm-and-matroska) | `.webm` and `.mkv` |
| [Sound](#sound) | M4A, MP3, WAV and AIFF, plus CAF, FLAC and other formats macOS plays |
| [Pictures](#pictures) | PNG, JPEG and HEIC, plus TIFF, GIF, BMP, HEIF and WebP |
| [LUTs](#luts) | `.cube` 3D LUTs |

Some of these only come in by a drop on the Media tab. See [Which way in](#which-way-in).

## Movies

Frame Job reads MOV, MP4, M4V and the other containers macOS plays. What matters is the video inside:

| Video | What Frame Job does |
| --- | --- |
| H.264, HEVC, ProRes, MJPEG, MPEG-4 | Reads it. |
| VP9 in MP4 | Reads Profile 0 and Profile 2, through macOS's optional decoder. Profiles 1 and 3 don't import. |
| AV1 | Reads it on an M3 or later Mac, because it needs a hardware decoder. |
| VP8 | Doesn't import. |

Before it adds a video, Frame Job decodes its first frame, so a file nothing on this Mac can decode is left out rather than added. An alert names the codec. See [Codecs this Mac can't decode](/projects/import-media/#codecs-this-mac-cant-decode).

The check gives up after 30 seconds, which usually means a stalled network volume. See [Import errors](/projects/import-media/#import-errors).

### Movies with alpha

Frame Job detects transparency when you import a movie. It recognises ProRes 4444, ProRes 4444 XQ and QuickTime Animation, and any track flagged as containing alpha, such as HEVC with alpha.

A **VP9 with Alpha (WebM)** file keeps its picture and loses its transparency when you bring it back in. To make a transparent clip you can re-import, export ProRes 4444 or HEVC with Alpha.

### Portrait and rotated movies

A movie imports at its display size, through the file's own rotation. A portrait phone clip comes in as 1080 × 1920, not as 1920 × 1080 lying on its side.

### Variable and unusual frame rates

Frame Job takes the rate macOS reports for the video track, which gives a variable-rate file one rate too.

A rate within 0.01 fps of a standard one becomes exactly that rate: 23.976, 24, 25, 29.97, 30, 48, 50, 59.94 or 60 fps. Anything else keeps three decimals, so a 47.3 fps screen recording isn't called 48.

If the file reports no rate, Frame Job works it out from the shortest frame. With nothing to go on, it uses 30 fps.

## WebM and Matroska

macOS can't open these, so Frame Job copies the streams unchanged into a QuickTime movie, with no re-encoding. It reads `.webm` and `.mkv` files with VP9, AV1, H.264 or HEVC video and Opus, Vorbis or AAC sound.

A file is recognised by its header, not its name, and the first video track and first audio track are the ones copied. See [WebM and Matroska files](/projects/webm-and-matroska/).

## Sound

M4A (AAC and ALAC), MP3, WAV and AIFF come in every way. Other formats macOS plays, such as CAF and FLAC, come in only by a drop on the Media tab.

### Any sample rate

Sound at any rate other than 48 kHz, 96 kHz included, plays from a hidden 48 kHz copy, so it stays aligned with its place on the timeline. This is automatic. The copies live in the temporary folder, outside the project, and are made again whenever they're needed.

### MP3 gapless start

Some MP3s begin with a short stretch of encoder delay that isn't part of the recording. When macOS leaves it in, Frame Job skips it at any sample rate, so the sound starts on time. Playback, the waveform, transcription, sync and a reversed clip all skip the same amount.

This applies to MP3 files. An MP3 track inside a `.mov`, `.mp4` or `.m4a` isn't trimmed.

## Pictures

PNG, JPEG and HEIC come in every way. TIFF, GIF, BMP, HEIF and WebP come in only by a drop on the Media tab.

A picture imports as a still with no length of its own, so a clip of it can run any duration. Its transparency and EXIF orientation are honoured.

Only a GIF's first image is read, so an animated GIF imports as a still.

### Deep and HDR stills

| The still is | What Frame Job does |
| --- | --- |
| Deeper than 8 bits a component, such as a 16-bit PNG or TIFF or a 10-bit HEIC | Draws it at 16-bit float, so its levels reach the picture. See [Precision and bit depth](/hdr/precision/). |
| Labelled HLG or PQ | Treats it by its own colour instead of as SDR. Display P3, BT.709 and BT.2020 primaries are recognised. See [How sources are read](/hdr/how-sources-are-read/#hdr-stills). |
| HEIC with an HDR gain map (ISO 21496-1 or Apple's) | Shows its full HDR in an HLG project. An SDR project and every thumbnail draw the base picture. |

A frame showing a deep still is saved deep as PNG or HEIC, never as JPEG. See [Save Frame](/export/save-frame/). GIF and Animated PNG exports stay 8-bit.

## LUTs

Frame Job reads `.cube` 3D LUTs, which you apply as a clip's [look](/color/luts/) or as a file's [Camera Log](/hdr/log-luts/).

- 3D only, so a 1D LUT is refused.
- `LUT_3D_SIZE` from 2 to 65.
- At most 32 MiB.

A `.cube` is imported, not opened. **File ▸ Open…** doesn't take one, and one dropped on the window or the Dock isn't imported. Use **File ▸ Add Media…** or a drop on the Media tab.

## Caption files

An `.srt` isn't media. Bring it in with **File ▸ Import Captions…**. See [Import captions](/captions/import-captions/).

Import reads SubRip only. WebVTT can be [exported](/captions/export-captions/) but not imported.

## Which way in

The **Add Media…** and **File ▸ Open…** panels list fewer types than a drop on the Media tab takes.

| Files | **File ▸ Add Media…** | **File ▸ Open…** | A drop on the Media tab |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Movies | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| M4A, MP3, WAV and AIFF | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| PNG, JPEG and HEIC | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| `.cube` LUTs | Yes | No | Yes |
| TIFF, GIF, BMP, HEIF and WebP | No | No | Yes |
| CAF, FLAC and other sound macOS plays | No | No | Yes |

A drop on the Media tab has no type filter, so any file is tried, and an agent's import takes the same files. **File ▸ Add Media…** and a drop on the Media tab add to the open project, and **File ▸ Open…** makes a new untitled project around the file. See [Import media](/projects/import-media/) and [Drop files to open them](/projects/open-a-project/#drop-files-to-open-them).

In the Finder, **Open With ▸ Frame Job** is offered for movies, M4A, MP3, WAV, AIFF, PNG, JPEG and HEIC files. Frame Job doesn't make itself the default app for any of them.

## Related

- [Import media](/projects/import-media/)
- [Export formats](/export/formats/)
- [Convert files with ffmpeg](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/)
- [Limits](/reference/limits/)

---
title: "The .framejob package"
description: "See what a saved project holds, which parts Frame Job can rebuild and which it can't, and what happens when you move or copy a package."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A Frame Job project is one `.framejob` package: a folder the Finder shows as one file. It holds your edit, its caches and, if you ask for them, copies of your footage.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['File ▸ Save', 'File ▸ Consolidate Media…']}
  keys="⌘S"
  tools={['save_project', 'consolidate_media']}
/>

## What a package is

| Inside | What it is | Can Frame Job rebuild it? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`project.json`](#projectjson) | The edit itself | No. A package needs it to open. |
| [`cache/`](#cache) | Thumbnails, waveforms, analyses and renders | Yes, though [cloud transcripts](#transcripts-are-worth-keeping) cost money. |
| [`media/`](#media) | Copies of your footage, only after **Consolidate Media…** | No. It may be the only copy. |
| [`graphics/`](#graphics) | Graphic modules, fonts, images and kept versions, only once you add a graphic | No. |

To look inside, Control-click the package in the Finder and choose **Show Package Contents**.

A project only ever saves as a `.framejob` package. A movie or a still is a separate step: see [Export](/export/formats/) and [Save Frame](/export/save-frame/).

A save writes the new package beside the old one and swaps it in, so a crash part-way through can't leave half a package.

:::caution
A save keeps only those four things. Any other file you put inside a package is dropped at the next save, autosaves included.
:::

## `project.json`

This is the edit itself: the canvas, media list, tracks, clips and markers. It's the only thing a package needs in order to open.

A project from any earlier version of Frame Job opens, and the next save writes it in the current format. A project from a newer build won't open, and the message asks you to update Frame Job. See [Open a project from another version](/projects/open-a-project/#open-a-project-from-another-version).

If `project.json` can't be read, the message says "*name* does not contain a readable project.json." See [When a project won't open](/projects/open-a-project/#when-a-project-wont-open).

## `cache/`

Everything here is something Frame Job can rebuild, so a package with a missing or damaged `cache/` still opens and redraws.

| Folder | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `thumbs/` | Filmstrip thumbnails |
| `peaks/` | Waveforms |
| `loudness/` | Loudness measurements |
| `speech/` | Voice detection |
| `sync/` | The analysis for [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/) |
| `transcripts/` | [Transcripts from AssemblyAI](#transcripts-are-worth-keeping) |
| `device-transcripts/` | Words recognised on this Mac |
| `analysis/` | [On-device analysis](/projects/media-analysis/): shot changes, faces, sound events and subjects found for an agent, the faces and subjects drawn by **View ▸ Show Subjects**, and the masks for **Remove Background** |
| `reversed/` | [Reversed clips](/speed/reverse/) |
| `ramp-audio/` | Sound for [speed ramps](/speed/speed-ramps/) |
| `isolated/` | [Voice Isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/) renders |
| `voiced/` | [Voice effect](/audio/voice-effects/) renders |

The per-file caches build in the background after an open, an import or a relink, and the timeline fills in as they finish. At most two files' sound caches build at a time. A cache that already matches its file is never rebuilt. Analyses and renders are made when something asks for them.

Masks are the largest of these: a minute of 1080p video's masks take about 62 MB.

### Transcripts are worth keeping

A transcript from AssemblyAI costs money to make again, so treat `cache/transcripts/` as worth keeping. Everything else in `cache/` rebuilds for nothing but time.

## `media/`

This folder exists only after [Consolidate Media…](/projects/consolidate-media/), and it holds copies of your footage. Unlike `cache/`, it may be the only copy, so don't delete it.

By default a project doesn't copy your footage. It remembers each file's path and a Finder bookmark, and reads the file from there. The package stays small but depends on the footage staying put. Consolidate Media is how a package comes to hold everything it needs.

## `graphics/`

This folder exists once you add a [graphic](/graphics/manage-graphics/). It holds the graphic modules and these folders:

| Folder | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `fonts/` | [Fonts](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/) the graphics use |
| `assets/` | [Images](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/) the graphics use |
| `history/` | The last 10 kept versions of each module, one folder per module |

## How a package travels

Moving, copying or consolidating a package keeps its caches. Until an untitled project is first saved, its caches live in a temporary folder, and the first save copies them in.

When you open a package, any media missing from its stored path is looked for in the package's own `media/` folder under the same name. That's what lets you move a consolidated package. A working link is never replaced this way.

A referenced file that has moved is often found again through its bookmark. If it isn't, see [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/).

To take a project to another Mac, run Consolidate Media first, so the footage goes with it.

## Related

- [Save, revert and close](/projects/save-and-revert/)
- [Consolidate Media](/projects/consolidate-media/)
- [Where Frame Job keeps its files](/reference/file-locations/)

<system-reminder>
Contents of /Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob/.claude/worktrees/help-docs/docs/site/CLAUDE.md:

# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, Node is pinned by `.node-version`. `README.md` has the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.
